status.en: 12 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 40% fewer than the week before, most of them in Tigray, Amhara and Addis Ababa.
status.nb: 12 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 40 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Tigray, Amhara og Addis Ababa.

summary.en: Mass killings of Orthodox Christians have resumed in Oromia, with attacks in Arsi killing at least 60 people and road-blockade incidents killing another 55, according to the Ethiopian church. TPLF senior commander John Medid was captured in central Tigray by forces linked to the TPLF. Over 35,000 people have fled the fighting across the border into Moyale, Kenya, prompting condemnation from regional leaders. The UN mission in Somalia has concluded while the UN food programme appointed a new head amid the renewed conflict. 2,824 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Massedrap på ortodokse kristne har gjenopptatt i Oromia, med angrep i Arsi som drepte minst 60 personer og veiblockader som drepte ytterligere 55, ifølge den etiopiske kirken. TPLF-seniorkommandør John Medid ble tatt til fange i sentrale Tigray av styrker knyttet til TPLF. Over 35 000 personer har flyktet fra kampene over grensen til Moyale i Kenya, noe som har ført til fordømmelse fra regionale ledere. FN-misjonen i Somalia er avsluttet mens FN-matprogrammet har utnevnt en ny leder midt i den fornyede konflikten. 2 824 dødsfall i kamp ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Fano insurgency
background.extract: The Fano insurgency is an armed conflict and insurgency in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia that began in April 2023 between the Fano militia and the Ethiopian government. The conflict started after the government attempted to dissolve the Amhara Special Forces and other regional forces as part of a plan to reform and centralize the country's security apparatus, and integrate them into the federal armed forces. This move led to protests and armed resistance by local forces under Fano.
